what_happened: Seeded the chronicle with 9 ground truths, 2 hypotheses, and 5 open threads by writing JSON files directly to ~/.sovereign/chronicle/. Used gt_/hyp_/ot_ prefixes for clarity. This worked but bypassed the ExperientialMemory API.
what_learned: When bulk-seeding chronicle data, writing JSON files directly is fine for bootstrapping. But for ongoing use, go through the API to ensure consistent format. The direct-write approach is a one-time bootstrap, not a pattern to repeat.

what_happened: Seeded chronicle data in session 2 using raw .json files dumped via bash. ExperientialMemory.recall_insights() reads .jsonl files in domain subdirectories (insights/<domain>/*.jsonl). The 11 seeded insights and 5 open threads were invisible to the API — claude.ai instance saw empty chronicle.
what_learned: Always write chronicle data through the ExperientialMemory API (record_insight, record_open_thread), never by hand. The API handles directory structure (domain subdirs) and file format (.jsonl). Data written outside the API is invisible to recall.

what_happened: recall_insights(domain="all") returned [] because "all" is truthy in Python. Code did insights_dir/"all"/*.jsonl - directory doesnt exist. get_open_threads worked because claude.ai happened to call it without a domain param.
what_learned: In MCP handlers, always normalize sentinel values. Treat domain="all" as domain=None. This is a common API design issue - callers will pass "all" to mean "no filter" but the backend interprets it literally as a domain name.

what_happened: POST /messages returned 503 through tunnel. Root cause: handle_post_message is a raw ASGI handler (scope, receive, send) that returns None. Starlette Route expected a Response object, tried to call None, crashed with TypeError. GET endpoints worked because SSE holds the connection open.
what_learned: MCP SSE transport handlers are ASGI-level, not Starlette-level. Use ASGI middleware to intercept /messages POST before Starlette routing. The pattern: class wrapping inner Starlette app, checking scope[path] and scope[method], delegating to handle_post_message directly.
